transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I’m constantly losing the tools and paperwork I need at work, and it’s starting to cause real problems on the line. I work at a meat processing plant, and misplacing things like my knives or temperature logs is starting to slow down production and get me into trouble with my supervisors.

Did you also have similar problems with inattention, forgetfulness, or losing things when you were a child or in school, and do these difficulties happen in more than one setting such as at work and at home?

Yes, absolutely. Even back in primary school, my teachers would write on my report cards that I daydreamed a lot, lost my worksheets, and struggled to follow directions. It definitely happens at home too, whether I'm constantly losing my keys, tuning out when my family is talking to me, or struggling to focus on my online study modules.
Before age 12, did these attention and forgetfulness problems clearly cause difficulties at school or at home, and have they continued without long breaks since then?

Yes, they definitely caused issues back then; my primary school teachers always wrote on my report cards that I was daydreaming, losing worksheets, and needing instructions repeated. It’s been a continuous, lifelong struggle for me, but it has really come to a head over the last couple of years with my increased responsibilities at the plant and the demands of my certification courses.
Do you also have problems with restlessness, fidgeting, interrupting others, or acting before thinking, or is it mainly inattention and losing things?

It is almost entirely about the inattention, spacing out, and constantly losing my things. I don't really experience restlessness, fidgeting, or interrupting people at all. My main struggles are just staying focused and keeping track of my tasks and tools.
Do you also have any difficulty organizing tasks, finishing work on time, or making careless mistakes because you miss details, or is it mainly just losing things and spacing out?

Yes, I definitely struggle with that. When I'm given a list of tasks at work, I often get sidetracked and leave things half-finished. Also, I frequently drift off during routine work and have to double-check everything because I'm afraid I've made a mistake or missed an important detail.
Do these attention problems happen even when the task is important or interesting to you, and do they still cause problems in several areas of your life?

Yes, even with things I really want to do, like my sustainable sourcing certification, I struggle to focus and keep putting off the reading because my brain just gets exhausted. It definitely affects multiple areas of my life, from slowing down the line at work because I've lost my tools, to misplacing my keys at home and having my family get frustrated when I tune out during conversations.
Have you ever had a lot of hyperactivity or impulsive behaviors, such as feeling unable to sit still, fidgeting, talking excessively, interrupting others, or acting without thinking?

No, I’ve never really struggled with hyperactivity or impulsivity like that. I don't have trouble sitting still, fidgeting, or interrupting people when they speak. My difficulties have always been almost entirely about losing my tools, spacing out, and struggling to keep my focus.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports a lifelong pattern of prominent inattention and disorganization with frequent losing of items, distractibility, incomplete tasks, and difficulty sustaining focus across multiple settings (work, home, study), with clear onset before age 12 and functional impairment. Hyperactivity and impulsivity are denied, making the predominantly inattentive presentation of ADHD the best fit.
